text:
kai: quick thread — noticed a p99 tail regression after the new kernel-selection change on x86 nodes. p50 unchanged but p99 jumped ~40ms on short sequences. anyone seen this?

maria: saw the spike in canary yesterday around 18:12 UTC. looks correlated with fused-attn kernel falling back to generic path for sequences <= 32 (we added the fallback last week).

james: KV cache hit rates are fine ~92%. not seeing client-side request size changes. this smells like microbatching + kernel choice interacting with scheduler queuing.

leo: +1. my hypothesis: when kernel chooses fused path for long sequences but falls back for short ones, the continuous-batcher groups those short requests differently -> more queue delay variance -> tail.

perf-bot: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/graph?panelId=512&from=now-6h

maria: i ran a quick profiler on a replica: CPU spin up spikes during kernel fallback, and observed small but frequent context switches at the batch boundary. attaching a sample log excerpt:```
[2026-02-10T18:12:04Z] batch_start tokens=24 microbatch_count=7 kernel=fused_attn fallback=true
[2026-02-10T18:12:04Z] schedule_delay_ms=12.4 kv_hit=true
[2026-02-10T18:12:04Z] kernel_load_time_ms=3.2 exec_ms=14.8
```

james: interesting — schedule_delay_ms=12.4 is non-trivial for our 50ms SLO. if microbatching is adding jitter, we should sweep `max_batch_tokens` and `max_wait_ms` to see the p95/p99 tradeoffs.

kai: proposed experiment: run two sweeps (A/B):
- Sweep A: fix max_batch_tokens = [256,128,64] with max_wait_ms=8
- Sweep B: fix max_wait_ms = [2,4,8,16] with max_batch_tokens=128
collect: p50/p95/p99, tail quantile hist, microbatch size distribution, kv_hit, kernel-fallback ratio.

leo: also include a run where we pin kernel selection to non-fused for sequences <=32 (force no-fallback) to see if unified kernel reduces queue variance.

maria: i'll enqueue jobs in perf-runner and tag them `microbatch-sweep-1779`. will capture perf traces + flamegraphs. expected runtime ~3h for full matrix.

james: small nit: when you sweep, please measure `batcher.max_inflight` too or at least monitor it. we've had spikes when in-flight exceeds 24. that amplifies tail.

kai: good call. add `max_inflight = [12,24,48]` to the matrix but limit permutations (two fixed combos) so we don't explode runtime.

perf-bot: perf-runner job created: job_id=pr-4821 start=2026-02-11T02:00:00Z

maria: starting first run now. will post results in this thread and drop the perf link.

leo: if we see that forcing non-fused improves p99 but hurts p50 too much, consider a dynamic policy: use kernel hint + queue-time threshold to decide fallback at runtime (if queue_delay > X, prefer the faster-latency kernel).

kai: action items:
- maria: run matrix and upload traces (due EOD PST)
- james: watch KV cache telemetry and in-flight counters during runs
- leo: prototype dynamic kernel hint heuristic if runs show improvement

maria: ack. starting run 1 (max_batch_tokens=256, max_wait_ms=8, max_inflight=24). will update with p95/p99 after first 30m window. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

james: thanks — i'll keep an eye on dashboard and disable canary if we regress to >60ms p99.

kai: thanks team. goal is to get p99 back under 35ms for short sequences without sacrificing throughput.
